title: Forecast with assumptions and uncertainty
goal: Calculate a reserve-aware forecast and recognize insufficient evidence.
challenge: Use the synthetic history to estimate reaching a 1000 MiB capacity with a 100 MiB reserve. State current sample day, growth assumptions, headroom and time units. Explain why the supplied irregular history cannot justify a reliable linear forecast.

steps.explanation: Create a unique private guest workspace. Retain its printed path; repeat starts a new workspace, never overwrites old evidence. Stop if creation/change-directory fails.
steps.expected: A new /home/learner/capacity-forecast.XXXXXX directory. All files below are guest-local.

steps.explanation: Create the same small synthetic history; do not substitute current df capacity.

steps.command: awk 'NR==2 {first_day=$1; first_used=$2} NR>1 {last_day=$1; last_used=$2} END {rate=(last_used-first_used)/(last_day-first_day); limit=1000; reserve=100; if(rate<=0) {print "insufficient positive trend"; exit 1}; remaining=limit-reserve-last_used; printf "rate=%g MiB/day; headroom=%g MiB; days_after_last=%g; threshold_day=%g\n",rate,remaining,remaining/rate,last_day+remaining/rate}' history.txt > forecast.txt; cat forecast.txt
steps.explanation: Compute with awk and independently check: (410-200)/21=10; (1000-100-410)/10=49. These are arithmetic estimates, not promises.
steps.expected: 490 MiB headroom; 49 days after day 21; threshold day 70. Without reserve, physical capacity would be reached on day 80.

steps.explanation: Type an insufficient-evidence case with changes -10, +110 and -90 MiB.
steps.expected: Endpoint growth alone masks reversals; do not claim its small positive average is reliable.

steps.explanation: Explain what additional samples, workload context or retention policy are needed.
steps.expected: Accept “insufficient evidence for a reliable forecast,” with reasons. A zero/negative trend also cannot establish a future exhaustion date.

hints: Usable threshold is capacity minus reserve, not full capacity.
49 days means after the last sample; day 70 is measured from day zero.
A mechanically calculated endpoint average can be mathematically correct and predictively unjustified.
review: I independently checked rate, headroom, days after the last sample and the absolute threshold day.
I rejected a reliable forecast for the irregular case and identified missing evidence.
coverage: Partial 200.2 reserve-aware prediction, assumptions and insufficient-evidence reasoning. Completion records self-review, not verified guest assessment; there is no score.
